conditions.name: Autism (ASD)[cite: 1]
conditions.description: Morton 2023 reframed the ASD signal away from single taxa toward a gut-brain metabolic architecture — amino-acid / carbohydrate / lipid profiles encoded largely by Prevotella, Bifidobacterium, Desulfovibrio and Bacteroides, with glutamate the strongest metabolite signal. Counterweight (Neuron 2025): classifiers cannot separate autistic children from their own siblings, and stool consistency (constipation/diarrhoea) confounds many case-control ASD taxa findings — so treat the single-taxon directions below cautiously.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: OCD[cite: 1]
conditions.description: A 2023 systematic review (Law et al.) and a dysbiosis-centred review (Bendriss et al.) corroborate this profile: OCD shows LOWER gut α-diversity (species richness/evenness) and the recurring pattern of increased Alistipes (Rikenellaceae) alongside depletion of Prevotellaceae and butyrate producers (Oscillospira, Odoribacter, Anaerostipes, Agathobacter, Coprococcus, Lachnospira) — with Lachnospira pectinoschiza depletion tracking obsession-subscale severity. Direction isn't settled: a saliva/blood study found Actinobacteria and Firmicutes raised, and a natural-OCD deer-mouse model showed increased Desulfovermiculus, Aestuariispira, Peptococcus, Holdemanella and families Lachnospiraceae/Ruminococcaceae (animal — and opposite to the human Lachnospiraceae depletion). Probiotic signal: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and L. casei attenuate OCD-like behaviour in rodents; no human RCT yet.[cite: 1]

down.note: Depletion of Lachnospira pectinoschiza correlated with OCD obsession-subscale severity (Domenech 2022); ↓ in the Law 2023 synthesis.[cite: 1]
2025 two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis found Ruminococcaceae has a protective causal effect against OCD.
Same 2025 MR study found Bilophila (Proteobacteria) also has a protective causal effect against OCD.

Common thread across studies: reduced α-diversity that scales with illness duration, and depletion of butyrate-producing Faecalibacterium/Roseburia/Coprococcus.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: Borderline Personality Disorder[cite: 1]
conditions.description: EVIDENCE BASE IS THIN. As of 2026, exactly one primary 16S study exists (Rössler 2022, n = 24 unmedicated BPD women vs 21 HC women — all-female cohort). Alpha- and beta-diversity did not differ between groups; the signal is at species level, in bacteria that produce or feed short-chain-fatty-acid pathways. Findings correlated with psychometric severity but have not yet been independently replicated. Male BPD, medicated BPD, and BPD with comorbidities (MDD, PTSD, eating disorders) are essentially unstudied. Treat everything here as directional, not established. The SCFA-depletion pattern is directionally consistent with what's seen in MDD, BD, and anxiety, which is unsurprising given the high comorbidity.[cite: 1]

up.note: B/F ratio elevated in BPD; approached but did not cross p < 0.05 (p = 0.06, r = 0.23). Directional finding — replication needed.[cite: 1]

down.note: Depleted as the denominator of the elevated Bacteroidetes/Firmicutes ratio (p = 0.06). Also parent phylum of the four significantly-depleted species below.[cite: 1]
Strongest species-level finding: p = 0.003, r = 0.41. SCFA-producing Firmicute. Correlated with BPD psychometric severity.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: Parkinson's disease[cite: 1]
conditions.description: The most robust, best-replicated gut-microbiome signal in neurology. The recurring pattern: mucin-layer-degrading Akkermansia up, SCFA/butyrate producers (Roseburia, Faecalibacterium, Lachnospiraceae, Blautia, Fusicatenibacter) down. Nishiwaki showed this holds across countries and is independent of constipation, BMI, sex, age and COMT-inhibitor use. Mechanistic throughline: butyrate loss + mucus-layer degradation → barrier permeability → enteric α-synuclein. Caveats: directions are for established PD; COMT inhibitors independently raise Lactobacillaceae, and disease stage shifts the picture (Faecalibacterium/Fusicatenibacter depletion predicts faster progression).[cite: 1]

up.note: Mucin-layer degrader; the single most consistent PD enrichment.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: ME/CFS[cite: 1]
conditions.description: Two simultaneous 2023 Cell Host & Microbe cohorts (Guo n=106/91; Xiong short- vs long-term). Core signal: loss of butyrate-producing capacity — F. prausnitzii and E. rectale depleted, with F. prausnitzii abundance inversely tracking fatigue severity, confirmed functionally by metagenomics, qPCR and fecal SCFA metabolomics. Xiong found dysbiosis pronounced in short-term (<4 y) disease but largely resolved in long-term (>10 y) patients who retained metabolic/clinical aberrations — so disease duration matters. Opportunistic species (R. gnavus, Enterocloster, Hungatella, Eggerthella) enriched.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: Fibromyalgia[cite: 1]
conditions.description: Well-controlled case-control (Minerbi 2019): 77 women with FM vs matched controls, with differences independent of diet, physical activity, medication and comorbid IBS, and taxa abundance tracking symptom severity. Signature is a reshuffle of the butyrate-producing community — the well-characterised 'healthy' producers (F. prausnitzii, B. uniformis, P. copri, Blautia faecis) depleted while less-characterised producers (Intestinimonas, Flavonifractor, Eisenbergiella, Butyricicoccus) rise, mirrored by altered serum SCFAs. Bifidobacterium and Eubacterium (neurotransmitter-metabolising genera) reduced — a plausible tie to the low-GABA / high-glutamate axis reported in FM.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: Migraine[cite: 1]
conditions.description: EVIDENCE IS ON MIGRAINE BROADLY, NOT VESTIBULAR MIGRAINE — no vestibular-migraine-specific microbiome study exists yet, so read this as an adjacent-population proxy. Direction varies by age (Roseburia reportedly UP in paediatric cases) and prophylactic medication shifts several genera — so treat these directional calls as tentative.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: PTSD[cite: 1]
conditions.description: EVIDENCE BASE IS THIN — small, heterogeneous, mostly phylum-level, with no consistent α/β-diversity difference. Anchored by one exploratory study (Hemmings 2017, n=18 PTSD + 12 trauma-exposed controls). The recurring finding is depletion of Actinobacteria, Lentisphaerae and Verrucomicrobia (the last includes barrier-supporting Akkermansia), with depletion tracking CAPS-5 symptom severity. Later cohorts (Malan-Müller 2022, Zeamer 2023) add genus-level signals but overlap poorly, and several cohorts are veteran/occupational, limiting generalisation.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: Anorexia nervosa[cite: 1]
conditions.description: IMPORTANT — most of these shifts are downstream of the semi-starved, low-BMI state itself, not a cause. Methanobrevibacter smithii tracks inversely with BMI, faecal SCFA excretion falls on a hypocaloric diet, and several changes partially (though often incompletely) renormalise with weight restoration. The one causal signal is Fan 2023, where transplanting AN microbiota into germ-free mice transferred an anorexia-like phenotype — so the microbiome may also feed back onto the illness. Functionally, gut-brain modules for serotonin biosynthesis and for dopamine / glutamate / tryptophan degradation are enriched in AN, a plausible route to mood and appetite effects. Evidence is heterogeneous (small cohorts, few at species level, starvation a massive confound) — read the taxa as an illness-state signature, not a target.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: Tourette syndrome[cite: 1]
conditions.description: EVIDENCE IS THIN AND INCONSISTENT — small, paediatric tic-disorder (TD/TS) cohorts, mostly single-centre, with no consensus on α- or β-diversity and taxa that move in opposite directions across studies; treat directions as tentative. The most reproducible signals are increased Bacteroides and Ruminococcus (Ruminococcus lactaris especially enriched in TS specifically) and decreased Bifidobacterium. A GABA thread runs through the data and may interest you: the GABA-degrading Klebsiella pneumoniae rises with symptom deterioration, while GABA-producing Bifidobacterium, Eubacterium and Akkermansia muciniphila are inversely correlated with tic severity (YGTSS) — yet, oppositely, some GABA-producing Bacteroides species (B. thetaiotaomicron, B. eggerthii, B. dorei) correlate positively with severity. Notable conflicts: one drug-naive-TD cohort (Wang 2022) found Prevotella and Faecalibacterium INCREASED, opposite to the depletion seen in most other conditions here, and Odoribacter is up in TD but down in OCD. A probiotic/FMT signal exists (Limosilactobacillus reuteri; small FMT case series) but no definitive RCT.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: Multiple sclerosis[cite: 1]
conditions.description: Autoimmune demyelinating CNS disease. The flagship iMSMS shotgun study (576 patients + genetically unrelated household controls) is the strongest dataset: it reports enrichment of Akkermansia muciniphila, Ruthenibacterium lactatiformans, Hungatella hathewayi and Eisenbergiella tayi, and depletion of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Blautia. The recurring theme is loss of butyrate producers (Faecalibacterium, Roseburia, Coprococcus, Butyricimonas) plus a mucin-degrader (Akkermansia) and methanogen (Methanobrevibacter) rise. Composition also shifts with disease-modifying therapy, so treatment status is a major confound.[cite: 1]

up.note: Mucin-layer degrader; the most reproducible MS enrichment across cohorts. A lower Bifidobacterium(adolescentis):Akkermansia(muciniphila) ratio tracks higher EDSS disability (PNAS 2025). Note: some progression studies report Akkermansia falling in progressors, so within-MS direction is context-dependent. Cross-ref: also the single most consistent Parkinson's enrichment.[cite: 1]

Enriched in MS (iMSMS shotgun). Cross-ref: Eisenbergiella (incl. E. tayi and E. massiliensis) is also ↑ in fibromyalgia (Minerbi) and rises in rodent learned-helplessness depression models — a recurring 'up' signal across pain / neuro-inflammatory conditions.[cite: 1]
Enriched in MS in the iMSMS shotgun cohort.[cite: 1]
Enriched in MS in the iMSMS shotgun cohort.[cite: 1]

Archaeal methanogen elevated in MS; correlates with elevated breath methane and proposed to enhance dendritic-cell recruitment. Cross-ref: methanogen overgrowth also appears in the SIBO workup of hEDS.[cite: 1]
Increased in disease-modifying-therapy-treated vs untreated MS patients (Jangi).[cite: 1]
Phylum-level increase reported in MS (contested across cohorts). Cross-ref: opposite direction to the ↓ Bacteroidetes seen in autism.[cite: 1]

down.note: Anti-inflammatory butyrate producer depleted in MS (iMSMS shotgun; an IgA-coated F. prausnitzii variant is also reduced at disease onset). Cross-ref: consistently ↓ in fibromyalgia, IBS and depression too — a shared 'loss of butyrate producers' theme.[cite: 1]

iMSMS reports depleted Blautia species in MS; the MS-associated Blautia wexlerae drives inflammation and a lower Bifidobacterium:Akkermansia ratio in mouse transfer (PNAS 2025). Caveat: some reviews report Blautia ↑ in MS — direction is contested. Cross-ref: Blautia is ↓ in autism as well.[cite: 1]

Depleted across ~8 MS studies and lower in progressors; tends to rise again on disease-modifying therapy. Individual Prevotella species (P. copri, P. buccalis) associate with higher MS severity, so genus-vs-species stories diverge. Cross-ref: Prevotella is also ↓ in autism and Parkinson's.[cite: 1]
Butyrate/SCFA producer depleted in MS.[cite: 1]
Butyrate producer depleted in MS. Cross-ref: Coprococcus ↓ is a recurring depression finding (Valles-Colomer).[cite: 1]
Depleted in MS; a lower Bifidobacterium:Akkermansia ratio tracks disability. Cross-ref: Bifidobacterium ↓ is shared with depression, autism and IBS.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: Ehlers-Danlos (hypermobile)[cite: 1]
conditions.description: Heritable connective-tissue disorder (defects in collagen / ECM). Gut involvement is real and common — chronic GI symptoms in ~80% — but it is a story of dysmotility, small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) and overlap with IBS/POTS/MCAS, NOT a characterised fecal taxon signature. There is currently no validated microbial biomarker for hEDS, so the entries here are deliberately sparse and flagged as indirect. Included because Kelsey's rheumatologist context makes the EDS/hypermobility axis relevant and because it cross-links strongly to IBS and fibromyalgia.[cite: 1]

up.note: Not a single taxon — overall small-bowel bacterial load. In hypermobility disorders (including hEDS) with GI symptoms, ~70% meet SIBO criteria on aspirate (≥10^3 CFU/mL); 100% of those with gastroparesis or dyssynergic defecation. Mechanism is connective-tissue-driven dysmotility allowing luminal microbes to proliferate, not a distinctive dysbiotic community.[cite: 1]

Facultative anaerobes proliferate under hypomotility/SIBO; this mirrors the IBS enrichment rather than being an EDS-specific finding, and is inferred from the SIBO / IBS-overlap literature rather than a case-control fecal study. Cross-ref: Enterobacteriaceae is also ↑ in IBS and depression.[cite: 1]

down.note: hEDS has no validated stool taxon signature. The literature is dominated by dysmotility/SIBO and very heavy overlap with IBS and functional foregut disorders (up to ~98% of hEDS patients meet criteria for a disorder of gut-brain interaction). Diagnostic microbial biomarkers have not been established — treat any species-level claim for EDS as provisional.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: Irritable bowel syndrome[cite: 1]
conditions.description: Disorder of gut-brain interaction; the most-studied gut condition here and a natural comparator for the neuropsychiatric set (IBS is highly comorbid with depression, anxiety, fibromyalgia, autism and hEDS). Pittayanon 2019's systematic review anchors the signature: ↑ Enterobacteriaceae, Lactobacillaceae and Bacteroides; ↓ uncultured Clostridiales I, Faecalibacterium (incl. F. prausnitzii) and Bifidobacterium. Diversity is decreased or unchanged. Subtype (IBS-C/D/M) matters — e.g. methanogens rise in constipation-predominant disease — and most studies cannot cleanly separate subtypes.[cite: 1]

up.note: Family-level enrichment (Proteobacteria) — facultative anaerobes favoured by inflammation and altered motility. One of the most reproducible IBS findings. Cross-ref: also ↑ in depression and (via SIBO) EDS.[cite: 1]
Genus increased in IBS overall (IBS-C in particular shows ↑ fecal Bacteroides); mixed across subtypes and some RCT meta-analyses find no difference.[cite: 1]
Family increased in IBS in the systematic review. Contrast: species-level Lactobacillus is often ↓ by qPCR in other meta-analyses — a level-of-resolution disagreement.[cite: 1]
Increased in several IBS cohorts (Firmicutes). Direction is not universal.[cite: 1]
IBS-enriched genus in the multicentre integrated analysis. Cross-ref: also enriched in endometriosis gut.[cite: 1]
Elevated (with Enterobacter) in the 23-study meta-analysis. Cross-ref: Escherichia-Shigella is ↑ in autism and endometriosis too.[cite: 1]
IBS-enriched genus (formerly within Clostridium) in the integrated multicentre analysis.[cite: 1]

down.note: Anti-inflammatory butyrate producer consistently depleted in IBS; a network hub species. Cross-ref: also ↓ in fibromyalgia, MS and depression.[cite: 1]
Depleted across most IBS cohorts (5/7 studies significant in Pittayanon). Cross-ref: Bifidobacterium ↓ is shared with depression, autism and MS.[cite: 1]
Uncultured Clostridiales I consistently decreased in IBS across European cohorts.[cite: 1]
Methanogens reduced overall in IBS vs controls — though a methane-positive, constipation-predominant (IBS-C / IMO) subtype is well recognised, so this reverses in that subgroup.[cite: 1]
Depleted in IBS in the pathophysiology review.[cite: 1]

conditions.name: Endometriosis[cite: 1]
conditions.description: Estrogen-dependent inflammatory disease (endometrial-like tissue outside the uterus); frequently comorbid with IBS. Two microbiomes matter — gut and reproductive tract — and the 'estrobolome' (gut microbes that deconjugate estrogens via β-glucuronidase) is the proposed mechanistic link. Gut findings (this atlas' focus): a higher Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio, phylum-level rises in Actinobacteria/Proteobacteria/Verrucomicrobia, loss of Lactobacilli and butyrate producers (Ruminococcaceae, Lachnospira), and severity-dependent shifts (Dialister ↓, Streptococcus/Lactobacillus ↑ with stage; Prevotella/Bacteroides ↓ in advanced disease). Directions are frequently contested between Shan 2020, Svensson 2021 and the 2025 meta-analysis, so several taxa here carry explicit caveats.[cite: 1]

up.note: Phylum enriched in the endometriosis gut (Shan 2020 and a 2019 systematic review).[cite: 1]
Phylum higher in the endometriosis gut; more patients show Shigella/Escherichia dominance.[cite: 1]
Phylum higher in the endometriosis gut (includes Akkermansia).[cite: 1]

Increased at genus level per the Iavarone review. Stage twist: in advanced / late-stage disease Prevotella (and Bacteroides) instead decrease. Cross-ref: Prevotella direction is strongly condition- and severity-dependent (↓ in autism/MS/PD).[cite: 1]
Enriched in the endometriosis gut (Shan 2020; Iavarone). Cross-ref: opposite to the Blautia ↓ seen in autism and MS.[cite: 1]
Enriched in the endometriosis gut (Shan 2020).[cite: 1]
Enriched, and rises with disease severity alongside Lactobacillus while Dialister falls. Cross-ref: Streptococcus is also IBS-enriched.[cite: 1]
More endometriosis patients show gut Shigella/Escherichia dominance. Cross-ref: Escherichia-Shigella is ↑ in autism and (as E. coli) in IBS.[cite: 1]

Severity twist: with increasing disease stage some studies report Lactobacillus (and Streptococcus) rising while Dialister falls — so 'low Lactobacillus' is the baseline signal, not a monotonic one.[cite: 1]
Reduced mucosa-adherent barrier taxon in endometriosis per the 2025 meta-analysis (Shan 2021). Contested: Shan 2020 reported Bifidobacterium ↑ — direction is not settled.[cite: 1]

Butyrate-producing family decreased in endometriosis — loss of anti-inflammatory SCFA capacity, a pattern shared with autoimmune dysbiosis. Cross-ref: Ruminococcaceae also ↓ in autism.[cite: 1]
Decreasing Dialister tracks increasing endometriosis severity (advanced stage, deep infiltrating disease, symptom burden). Cross-ref: Dialister is ↓ in depression and autism as well.[cite: 1]
Decreased in the endometriosis gut (Shan 2020).[cite: 1]
Decreased in advanced / late-stage endometriosis microbiomes; advanced disease is instead marked by enrichment of Bartonella and Snodgrassella and suppressed steroid-biosynthesis pathways.[cite: 1]
